text:
BUF arrives with the better underlying game. At five on five the Sabres have taken 55% of the expected goals this season, while TOR sits at 43%, and the gap shows in prevention: BUF allows 2.84 expected goals per 60 to TOR's 3.77, with nearly identical creation (3.03 against 3.00). The model sees the game as close anyway, at 3.13 expected goals for BUF and 3.08 for TOR. On special teams, TOR's power play (0.77 expected goals a game) meets a BUF penalty kill that allows exactly 0.77, and the Leafs take 4.14 penalties a game, which keeps feeding opponents.

In net, projected starter Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen is at -3.84 goals saved above expected this season (.850), though he was +9.12 over 35 games last year. Projected TOR starter Sergei Bobrovsky is the reverse: +4.65 (.907) over four games this year after a -13.5 mark across 52 games last season. Early results favor Toronto's goalie, the longer record favors Buffalo's.

Both teams are 2-2-1 in their last five, but BUF averaged 49% of the expected goals in that stretch to TOR's 44%. Buffalo's most recent game was a 3-4 shootout loss at MTL where it held only 38%. Toronto came off a 4-5 loss at UTA, where it had 55%. Tage Thompson (39% to score, 27% for two or more points) leads Buffalo's list. For Toronto, William Nylander and Auston Matthews both sit at 38% to score and 30% for two or more points.
